A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LuCA/TOSCA research despite the changed title and publication format. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable matching.

before.justification: v1 reports original six-benchmark experiments, runtime and parameter comparisons, and component and hyperparameter ablations, including additional results in Appendix A.2.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds EuroSAT evaluation, task-wise accuracy, representation analyses and module-selection measurements in the main text and appendix.

M1.justification: Both versions use an adapter followed by a calibrator, one sparse module per task on the final CLS representation, a frozen backbone, cross-entropy plus l1 regularization, and entropy-based module selection. Expanded inference explanations and more explicit pseudocode do not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds a dedicated EuroSAT satellite-imagery classification scenario with ten classes, extending evaluation to an explicitly different image domain while retaining the six original benchmarks. Table 3 and Figure 5 report this additional coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1 and A add RanPAC across all six retained benchmarks and HiDePrompt on CIFAR, CUB and ImageNet-R with both backbones. Both also enter the runtime comparison. RanPAC was cited but not evaluated in v1; HiDePrompt is not evaluated on the other benchmark columns, which contain dashes.

E3.justification: v2 adds per-task accuracy evaluation, module-selection accuracy against ground-truth task identities, cosine-similarity comparisons and feature-separation diagnostics. EuroSAT uses B0 Inc2. Existing backbone choices, training budgets and hyperparameters remain unchanged. The stated VTAB class count changes from 100 to 50, matching v1's plotted range without establishing that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds direct investigations of single-token plasticity, satellite-domain robustness, module decorrelation under different regularization strengths, feature geometry and entropy-based routing reliability (Tables 2, 3 and B; Figures 5–7). The original hyperparameter and component-order ablations remain; LuCA_r becoming TOSCA_r is a rename.

E5.justification: Both versions state five random-seed runs and retain mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting in the main benchmark tables. However, v2 removes v1's explicit class-order seed of 1993. There is no documented increase in repeated runs or addition of confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Substantial new results include CUB task-wise average accuracy of 97.6% and EuroSAT task-wise average accuracy of 99.3% for TOSCA, alongside new baseline and diagnostic results. Retained TOSCA entries also change: ImageNet-R/IN21K final accuracy is revised from 78.28 to 79.28 in Table 1, and OmniBenchmark/IN1K from 78.65 to 79.65 in Table A. Other shared table entries remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The background prompt objective in Equation (2) changes its optimization variables from prompts, keys and the feature extractor to prompts, keys and classifier W, correcting its inconsistency with the frozen-backbone description. TOSCA's theoretical statements and Equations (10)–(11) are retained in Appendix A.1; no new proof is added.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain LuCA, sparse final-CLS adaptation through TOSCA, the stability–plasticity argument, and the headline accuracy and efficiency advantages. The continual-post-training framing and additional evidence do not materially redefine these scientific claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations connecting sparsity to reduced feature overlap and explaining why adaptation before calibration improves class geometry. It interprets task-wise and EuroSAT findings as evidence of plasticity and robustness. Appendix A.2 newly discusses lower IN1K average accuracies as an efficiency–adaptability tradeoff; dependence on pretrained-model generalization was already acknowledged in v1.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a code-repository link, explicitly identifies sigmoid calibration, and clarifies classifier optimization in Algorithm 1. Hardware and principal hyperparameters are retained. Conversely, it omits v1's explicit class-shuffling seed and statement that all methods use identical training/testing splits.

R1.justification: v2 adds HiDePrompt, EuroSAT and two sparse/online continual-learning references, and expands discussion of the already-cited RanPAC. It removes the squeeze-and-excitation analogy and citation, plus references to NISPA and continual prune-and-select. Positioning shifts toward foundation-model continual post-training while most related-work coverage remains.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, methodology discussion and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Neuroscience motivation moves into the introduction, theoretical underpinnings move to Appendix A.1, terminology changes throughout, and the experimental narrative is reorganized into more focused subsections, including a separate discussion of the existing joint-training comparison.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 2, 3 and B and Figures 5–7, expands existing benchmark tables and plots with additional comparators, and revises legends and captions. The LuCA diagram is redrawn, and the document adopts journal typography, headers and wider layouts. These are substantial display changes beyond numerical updates.

improvement.justification: v1 mainly supported its orthogonality, routing and single-token plasticity claims through aggregate accuracy and basic ablations. v2 directly investigates these properties through task-wise results, representation analyses and Appendix Table B, while adding a dedicated satellite-domain test and stronger comparator coverage. This substantially strengthens empirical scrutiny of the central design. Some formalization and experimental-detail gaps remain, and the class-order seed disclosure is lost, but these limitations do not outweigh the targeted evidential gains.
